xBRIEFInfo.description: P0 host-hook bridge, direct write denial, project deposit, and health reporting for issue #2438

plan.title: feat(harness): deft-hook P0 host PreToolUse enforcement and project deposit

narratives.Description: Ship Directive's P0 Tier-1 host-hook surface: a provider-neutral hook dispatcher, direct write-tool denial backed by the existing gated session ritual and active/running xBRIEF predicates, idempotent project deposits, and doctor/verify registration health.
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive user, I want the agent host to refuse direct file writes until the existing implementation gates pass, so advisory workflow rules cannot be silently bypassed before the working tree is modified.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Add a small normalized hook event/decision contract and CLI dispatcher for SessionStart and PreToolUse. 2. Extract a read-only ritual-state inspector from the existing verifier and compose it with the canonical xBRIEF preflight evaluator; do not create a second policy stack. 3. Add host codecs/deposits for the P0 project surfaces and wire them through init/update. 4. Extend hook health reporting and doctor without changing existing git-hook defaults. 5. Cover allow/deny, malformed input, idempotent merge, and doctor status. Explicitly defer compact re-arm (#2113), path/shell/MCP policy (#1394), and plugin packaging (#2369).
narratives.Origin: GitHub issue #2438 under epic #2437; implementation scope locked by operator on 2026-07-14.
narratives.Acceptance: 1. Hook dispatcher accepts stdin JSON and emits host-native allow/deny for direct write tools. 2. Missing/stale gated ritual or no active/running xBRIEF denies a write with actionable remediation. 3. Project deposit is idempotent and doctor reports registration health. 4. SessionStart is non-blocking. 5. No compact, path-policy, routing, or plugin-packaging work lands.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a supported host event on stdin, when hook:dispatch runs, then it normalizes the event and returns a deterministic allow or deny decision in the host's required response shape.
Given a direct write tool, when the gated ritual is stale or no active/running xBRIEF passes canonical preflight, then the host refuses the tool and names the recovery commands.
Given directive init/update runs, when host hook files are deposited, then Directive-owned entries are present without overwriting unrelated user configuration and a second run is a no-op.
Given a project with installed, missing, or drifted agent hooks, when the health probe runs, then it reports the registration state separately from existing git-hook health.
Given the P0 test matrix, when focused tests run, then allow, deny, malformed input, deposit idempotence, and health-reporting branches are covered.

expected_outputs: Direct write denial backed by canonical predicates
swarm.missing_traces_justification: Issue #2438 is the approved P0 implementation record; the affected surface is framework-internal harness infrastructure.
